label: ciliolate
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing a fringe of minute hairs. NOTE: Diminutive of ciliate; PATO:0001408 ciliated is a cellular quality (cilia as organelles) and does not apply.
reason: Floras use 'ciliolate' and 'microciliolate' for a fringe of minute marginal hairs. Neither PATO nor the FLOPO value terms have a term for it or for 'ciliate'; if a ciliate class is added, this should become its child.
'couleur blanche', 'blanco', 'blancas' = white; the word 'color' adds nothing.
'filament as long as the anther' compares one length with another part's length: the equality case of pattern 10, with the anther (PO_0009066) as the other part.
Hypocrateriform is already an exact synonym of FLOPO:0991144 salverform; this is the Latin, Spanish or French spelling.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: qualitative_value_relation between linear PATO_0001199 and elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: A hyphenated compound of two shape values, handled as a continuum like 'linear-lanceolate'.
'non aigus', 'apex not acute', 'ápice no agudo' negate PATO:0000389 acute.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: oblong PATO_0000946 and heart shaped PATO_0000948)
reason: A compound of two existing shape values. The 'oblan-céolé' example is a mis-split of 'oblancéolé' and should not be matched to this word.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: attenuate PATO_0001982 with obtuse PATO_0001935 at the tip)
reason: The apex narrows gradually (attenuate) to a blunt end (obtuse); both values exist and a single term would duplicate them.
'with a raised line' on a blade or axis is a thin longitudinal ridge. In 'Stipules a raised line' the stipules may be reduced to an interpetiolar line, which is better left unannotated.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer vascular bundle PO_0005020 part of the described organ; quality purple PATO_0000951)
reason: The word joins a part (vein) and a colour; it is the colour of the veins of the lip or petal, with the organ as the whole (slot 1, part of the bearer).
Negates the existing value FLOPO:0991174 gland-dotted.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer: apex of the part; two values: triangular PATO_0001875 and acute PATO_0000389)
reason: A part (apex) with two separate shape values, written as two annotations on the apex, not one term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: triangular PATO_0001875 and lanceolate PATO_0001877)
reason: A compound of two shape values; deltate is already mapped to triangular (rule C226).
A truncated piece of 'laxly few- to many-flowered': an indefinite flower count plus the lax quality (rule C169) on the inflorescence.
A double-edged stem is two-edged, an existing synonym of FLOPO:0991345 ancipitous. The Spanish 'cupule con borde doble' (double rim) is a different sense and should not take this rule.
States where the bearer is widest, not a shape such as ovate. docs/annotation-context-patterns.md lists the position of greatest width as a case not yet handled.
Parchment-like: thin, dry and fairly stiff, the texture glossaries treat with chartaceous, which is an exact synonym of PATO:0104010. Too few statements for a separate class.
A noun for a protuberance on a fruit or tooth, meaningless without its position. It is neither a part with a PO class nor a quality; 'with central hump' could at most be read as gibbous.
A laxly flowered inflorescence has its flowers loosely spaced: the 'lax' rule C169, PATO:0001802 loose.
A hyphenated spelling of the existing FLOPO:0991212 monomorphic.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: lanceolate PATO_0001877 and ovate PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid)
reason: A compound of two shape values.
'with colleters' says the part bears colleters; the class FLOPO_0986023 colleter exists.
A rachis bearing a crest; 'crenate' only describes the crest's edge, and FLOPO:0991196 crested already covers an irregular or toothed ridge.

target: tympaniform (FLOPO value class; id to confirm)
reason: A kettledrum-shaped fruit in outline is tympaniform (drum-shaped), which exists as a FLOPO value class. Its ID was not looked up in this review and must be confirmed in config/flopo_flora_value_terms.tsv before use.
Negates FLOPO:0991070 discolorous: the nerves are not a different colour from the blade.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer: margin of the sepal; two values: scabrous FLOPO:0991058 and ciliate)
reason: A margin that is both minutely scabrid and ciliate, best written as two values on the margin. The ciliate half needs the 'ciliolate' class proposed for 'microciliate'.
Gritty bark slash, tuber tissue and seed shell feel granular because of stone cells or crystals: PATO:0001759 granular.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: oblanceolate PATO_0002330 and spatulate PATO_0001937)
reason: A compound of two shape values.

Flushed with red = tinged red. The colour classes have the 'flushed' values (for example FLOPO_0980110 flushed with pink); reddish (FLOPO_0980086), a colour class rather than a 0991xxx value class, is the nearest for red.
'Semi-' weakens procumbent the way '±' does: the approximate-value pattern with PATO:0002389, not a new term.
